title: model catalog: add capability filters, compatibility flags, pricing & limits to listing endpoints
author: Priya Karthik
description: Motivation: expose richer model catalog metadata and filter/query surface to support product features (filter by capability, surface OpenAI compatibility aliases, and surface pricing/limits) and to enable routing/selection logic in the API gateway. This PR introduces capability flags on model metadata, new query parameters on the /models listing endpoint, and additional pricing/limits fields in the model payload. Checklist: - [x] Add capabilities field to model metadata and migration - [x] Add GIN index for capability array to support efficient filters - [x] Add openai_compatible and openai_aliases flags and alias mapping in OpenAI compatibility layer - [x] Expose price_per_1k_tokens and max_context_tokens on model objects - [x] Add API query params: capabilities (comma-separated), openai_compatible (bool), openai_aliases (bool) - [x] Add unit/integration tests and docs updates - [x] Add migration script and rollout guidance API changes (summary): - GET /models now accepts optional query params: capabilities (csv), openai_compatible (true|false), openai_aliases (true|false), and price_tier (basic|pro|enterprise). - Response model object additions: capabilities (array of strings), compatibility_flags (comma-separated string for quick search), openai_compatible (boolean), openai_aliases (array of strings, returned only when openai_aliases=true), price_per_1k_tokens (string USD decimal), max_context_tokens (integer as string in response). Implementation notes: - Catalog schema: added capabilities (text[]) and pricing JSON blob in metadata; migration script located at internal/catalog/migrations/20260220_add_capabilities.sql. - Indexing: added GIN index on capabilities to avoid full-table scans for common capability filters; documented expected cardinality in catalog.go. - OpenAI compatibility: introduced a lightweight alias map in pkg/openai_compat/alias_map.go which maps Redwood model IDs to common OpenAI aliases (e.g., rw-gpt-3.5 -> gpt-3.5-turbo-compat). openai_aliases are only returned when explicitly requested to avoid accidental leakage of compatibility mappings. - Backward compatibility: existing clients will continue to receive model objects; pricing/limits fields will be nil/missing for models not migrated yet. Clients should tolerate absent fields. - Migration and rollout: migration script can be run asynchronously; new fields are idempotent and safe to add. Feature flag redwood.catalog.filters controls UI rollout. Tests and CI: - Added unit tests for catalog filters and alias mapping. - Integration tests for /models with various filter combinations. - First CI run showed a flaky streaming test in the streaming suite; reran pipeline and all checks passed. Docs: - Updated docs/api/model-catalog.md with examples for new params, OpenAI alias behavior, and migration notes. Performance: - Benchmarked listing with capability filters on a 500k model synthetic catalog; with GIN index we saw <50ms median additional latency for typical queries; documented in perf notes. Rollout plan: - Merge to main, deploy API with new endpoint handling behind a compatibility flag, run migration in batches, enable feature flag for UI consumers after 95% of models have pricing metadata. Related work: Linear ENG-2419 (model catalog filters), ENG-2460 (openai compatibility mapping), PM-178 (product requirements). Support ticket SUP-4321 requested pricing exposure for billing reconciliation. Notes for reviewers: pay attention to migration idempotency, index creation during peak hours, and alias privacy semantics.

release_notes: Added capability filters and compatibility flags to model listing endpoints. New query params: capabilities (comma-separated), openai_compatible (bool), openai_aliases (bool). Models now return pricing keys price_per_1k_tokens and max_context_tokens. Backward compatible: existing clients will still see models but without pricing/limits fields until the next metadata migration. Rollout: gradual: catalog migration can be run asynchronously; UI will enable filters behind feature flag.
